title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Copilot Credits usage report for pay-as-you-go in Copilot Chat
summary: The briefing passes: the report paths, billing prerequisites, privacy control and qualified beta API call are supported by Microsoft documentation. The rollout dates and automatic default match Microsoft's supplied notice, and no actionable contradiction or unsupported claim was found.

claims.claim: Copilot Cost Management reports usage for supported services governed through Microsoft 365 spending policies.
claims.quote: Use Copilot > Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center when you want to manage and monitor Copilot Credit usage for services governed by Microsoft 365 usage-based billing policies.

claims.claim: Learn does not present Cost Management as a replacement for the Copilot Chat Credits report.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Credits report administrative configuration Cost Management supported services; read Credits report, Monitor Copilot Credit spending, billing comparison and Manage Copilot Studio costs. None describes replacing the Copilot Chat Credits report.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go usage can take 24 hours to appear in Azure Cost Management.
claims.quote: To view costs in the Azure portal ... Billed amounts are updated daily and sometimes more frequently. It can take 24 hours after usage of a service to show in Microsoft Cost Management.

claims.claim: Azure Cost Management provides a billing-oriented view.
claims.quote: Shows billing-oriented cost data, such as costs by subscription, service, resource, meter, or invoice period.

claims.claim: Azure Cost Management lacks the same user-level context as the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: It doesn't show the same user-level or spending-policy context as the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Azure Cost Management lacks the same spending-policy context as the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: It doesn't show the same user-level or spending-policy context as the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The Credits report is not a general report of all Copilot Studio agent consumption.
claims.quote: The Credits used metric shows the total credits used from interactions by users in your organization who don't have a Microsoft Copilot license and are interacting with agents in Copilot Chat that spin the Copilot Studio meter

claims.claim: Copilot Chat usage appears in the report when pay-as-you-go was configured in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: You can set up the pay-as-you-go billing policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center or Power Platform admin center. If you configure pay-as-you-go, and users without a Microsoft Copilot license use metered agents in Copilot Chat, the data appears in the report.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Usage reports hide usernames, display names, groups and sites by default.
claims.quote: By default, user-specific information like usernames, display names, groups, and sites is hidden in usage reports.

claims.claim: Usage Summary Reports Reader can view usage reports without user details.
claims.quote: To view usage reports, you must have one of the following permissions: ... Usage Summary Reports Reader (with no user details).

claims.claim: The report's alert user details can be exported to CSV.
claims.quote: Select View Copilot credits details to see the user list and export it to CSV.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Agent design influences the credits consumed.
claims.quote: The number of credits used depends on the design of the agent, how often users interact with it, and the features the agent uses.

claims.claim: Learn's example assigns 10 credits to tenant graph grounding in a response to one complex prompt.
claims.quote: an agent grounded in a tenant graph could use 12 credits (10 credits for tenant graph-grounding, and two credits for generative answers) to respond to a single complex prompt from a user.

claims.claim: Learn's example adds two credits for generative answers in that response.
claims.quote: an agent grounded in a tenant graph could use 12 credits (10 credits for tenant graph-grounding, and two credits for generative answers) to respond to a single complex prompt from a user.

claims.claim: Name concealment is at Settings > Org settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote: select Settings. ... Select Org Settings. ... On the Services tab, select Reports. ... In the Reports panel, uncheck the checkbox next to Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/admin/reportSettings updates tenant report concealment through displayConcealedNames.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/reportSettings ... { "displayConcealedNames": true }

claims.claim: Setting displayConcealedNames to true conceals user, group and site names.
claims.quote: If set to true, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites.

claims.claim: Setting displayConcealedNames to false shows identifiable information.
claims.quote: If false, all reports show identifiable information.

claims.claim: The printed report-settings endpoint is beta and not supported for production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The tenant concealment setting also hides or shows the Credits report's Billing Policy ID.
claims.quote: By default, the Copilot credits report anonymizes the Billing Policy ID, just like the username and display name. ... Changes to this hidden data setting affect the username, display name, and Billing Policy ID.

claims.claim: No additional report-specific administrative configuration is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Copilot Credits report administrative configuration settings enable disable report; read Credits report, usage reports overview and reporting options. Found setup prerequisites, report access, filters and concealment, but no additional report-specific administrative setting.
